missing_supported_requirements.why_missing_despite_evidence: Section states it presents information that could affect prospects, but only provides climate-related risks; it does not cover 'all sustainability-related risks and opportunities' (including opportunities) that could affect cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital across short/medium/long term.

No explicit disclosure that additional information has been provided where specifically applicable IFRS SDS requirements are insufficient, nor a clear linkage to effects on cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital over short/medium/long term.

Reporting period is stated, but the section does not state that the sustainability disclosures are for the same reporting entity as the related financial statements (eg, group vs parent, consolidation boundary).

Section asserts connected information across governance/strategy/risk/metrics, but does not explain connections across sustainability disclosures and other general purpose financial reports (eg, related financial statements) or provide cross-references.
Section does not identify the specific financial statements to which the sustainability-related financial disclosures relate (eg, consolidated financial statements for year ended 31 Dec 2024).

Section provides emissions data-quality composition, but does not state that data and assumptions are consistent (to the extent possible) with those used in the related financial statements or explain alignment where relevant.
Section states disclosures are presented in EUR, but does not state that EUR is the presentation currency of the related financial statements.
No statement that SASB Standards disclosure topics were considered (or concluded not applicable).

No explicit statement that the entity applied the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard(s) that specifically apply to the identified sustainability-related risks/opportunities (eg, IFRS S2 for climate).
No disclosure describing the judgement process used when no specific IFRS SDS applies, nor how information selected is relevant to user decision-making.
No disclosure describing how the judgement process ensures faithful representation when no specific IFRS SDS applies.
No statement that SASB metrics were considered when applying judgement under paragraph 57 (or concluded not applicable).

Section mentions NGFS v4 scenarios and a 5x5 risk matrix, but does not identify the specific standards/pronouncements/industry practice and other guidance applied in preparing the disclosures (including any SASB topics, if applicable).
No identification of the industry/industries guidance applied (IFRS/SASB/other) in preparing disclosures and identifying applicable metrics.
No cross-referencing is used or, if intended, no disclosure of cross-reference mechanics/locations consistent with B45–B47.
Section states the reporting period end date, but does not state that disclosures are reported at the same time as the related financial statements.

Section provides methodologies (risk matrix; scenario approach) but does not explicitly identify the most significant non-estimation judgements made in preparing the disclosures and their effect on information included.
Section provides emissions data-quality composition but does not identify which disclosed amounts are subject to a high level of measurement uncertainty.
Section provides data-quality composition but does not describe sources of measurement uncertainty (eg, value chain data availability/quality, model dependence) for each high-uncertainty amount.

required_fixes: Expand scope from climate-only risks to all material sustainability-related risks and opportunities (or clearly state scope and include opportunities), and link them to effects on cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital over short/medium/long term (IFRS_S1_3_C01, IFRS_S1_17_C01 alignment).
Add explicit identification of the related financial statements (which set, consolidated/parent, period) and confirm the same reporting entity boundary (IFRS_S1_20_C01, IFRS_S1_22_C01).
State that EUR is the presentation currency of the related financial statements (IFRS_S1_24_C01).
Add a statement on consistency of key data/assumptions with those used in the related financial statements (to the extent possible) (IFRS_S1_23_C01).

Describe connections across sustainability disclosures and other general purpose financial reports (eg, financial statements), including cross-references where relevant (IFRS_S1_21_C04; and if cross-referencing is used, comply with IFRS_S1_63_C01).

Include the required 'sources of guidance' disclosures: whether SASB topics/metrics were considered and what other standards/guidance were applied; identify relevant industry guidance used (IFRS_S1_55_C01, IFRS_S1_58_C01, IFRS_S1_59_C01, IFRS_S1_59_C02).
Add disclosures on significant judgements (non-estimation) made in preparing the sustainability disclosures (IFRS_S1_74_C01).
Strengthen measurement uncertainty disclosures by identifying high-uncertainty amounts and describing sources of uncertainty for each (IFRS_S1_78_C01, IFRS_S1_78_C03).
State whether sustainability disclosures are reported at the same time as the related financial statements (IFRS_S1_64_C01).

Add an explicit statement addressing whether additional information was necessary beyond specifically applicable IFRS SDS requirements to enable users to understand effects on cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital (IFRS_S1_15_C02).
ifrs_coverage_judge.summary: The section covers reporting period, currency, comparative periods, some climate risk descriptions, and some methodology/data-quality elements. However, multiple supported IFRS S1 general requirements are not met: it does not identify the related financial statements or confirm the same reporting entity boundary; it does not address connections to the financial statements; it lacks required disclosures about sources of guidance (including SASB consideration); it does not provide the required measurement-uncertainty structure (identify high-uncertainty amounts and sources); and it does not broaden to all sustainability-related risks and opportunities or clearly link them to cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital across time horizons.

unsupported_claims.claim_text: The disclosures are prepared to enable users to understand connections between governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: This is an intent/quality assertion about how the disclosures are prepared. The provided payload evidence lists governance, risk register and scenario notes, but does not evidence that the disclosures as presented actually enable understanding of the stated connections (e.g., explicit cross-references, mapping between governance/strategy/risk/metrics).

questionable_claims.claim_text: The disclosures present sustainability-related information that could reasonably be expected to affect the bank’s prospects.
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Materiality/fair presentation is asserted but not evidenced in the excerpt (no materiality assessment process, thresholds, or demonstration of completeness/neutrality). This is more of a compliance assertion than a verifiable fact from the provided evidence.

questionable_claims.claim_text: These sustainability-related financial disclosures are prepared for the reporting period ending 31 December 2024 and are presented in EUR.
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Period end and reporting currency are supported by payload (bank.fiscal_year_end; bank.reporting_currency). However, the statement could be read as asserting EUR is the presentation currency for the sustainability disclosures/financial statements without explicitly tying it to the financial statements’ presentation currency; evidence only supports a reporting currency field.

questionable_claims.claim_text: Comparative information is provided for 2022 and 2023.
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Comparative years are supported (metadata.comparative_years), but the excerpt does not evidence that comparatives are actually presented consistently (same measurement bases/definitions) across periods; it is a high-level assertion.

questionable_claims.claim_text: Scenario analysis applies NGFS v4 scenarios to the banking book; methodology includes a top-down sector-pathway approach with carbon price assumptions mapped to counterparty NACE sectors and stranded asset estimates derived from sector-level fossil fuel capex exposure; scope covers lending book exposures across DE, FR, IT, NL, ES; resilience assessments are performed under orderly and disorderly transition scenarios.
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Methodology notes are supported (climate_scenarios[*].methodology_notes) and resilience narrative exists (climate_scenarios[*].resilience_assessment). However, the draft excerpt does not include the resilience assessment statements themselves, and key methodological specifics (e.g., actual carbon price values, quantified outputs) are not evidenced within the section text.

required_fixes: For GR-009, either remove/soften the claim (e.g., 'The disclosures include information intended to help users understand connections...') or add explicit, verifiable linkage evidence in the section (cross-references/mapping showing how governance links to strategy, risk register items, and metrics/targets).

For GR-003, add a brief description of the materiality assessment approach used (process, criteria, governance, and how completeness/neutrality/accuracy were ensured) or rephrase as a policy statement rather than a factual assertion.

For GR-001, clarify what 'presented in EUR' refers to (reporting currency for these sustainability disclosures and/or the financial statements presentation currency) and align wording to the evidenced fields.
For GR-002, if keeping the claim, add a sentence confirming comparatives are prepared on a consistent basis (or disclose any changes in methods/definitions between 2022–2024).

For GR-012, if the section is meant to evidence resilience assessments, include a short, attributable summary of the orderly/disorderly resilience conclusions and key assumptions (or cross-reference where those results are disclosed).
evidence_judge.summary: Most factual items (period end, currency field, risk register items/ratings, monitoring frequencies, and data-quality percentages) are supported by the provided payload. However, the section contains at least one unsupported quality/intent claim about connected information (GR-009) and several compliance-style assertions (materiality/fair presentation, comparatives consistency, and scenario-analysis completeness) that are not fully evidenced within the section as written.

voice_issues: Voice is generally neutral and formal, but it does not consistently use standards-oriented verbs (e.g., 'disclose', 'prepare', 'assess') to frame statements as disclosures.
Mix of descriptive narrative and risk-register style bullets without an explicit basis-of-preparation framing sentence for each subsection, which weakens the assurance-like disclosure voice.
Some phrasing (e.g., 'could damage brand and trigger client attrition') reads more like risk commentary than structured IFRS-style disclosure language.
structure_issues: Headings are unnumbered and do not follow the requested numbered hierarchy (e.g., 1, 1.1, 1.2) aligned to IFRS S1/S2 pillars and general requirements.
Subsections do not consistently start with a one-sentence purpose statement explaining what is being disclosed and why it matters for users.

Bulleted risk list under 'Fair presentation and material sustainability-related information' is not preceded by an explicit lead-in sentence that frames it as an example set or subset of material climate-related risks.

The section does not follow the requested layered structure (overview paragraph → structured bullets/tables → brief interpretation and cross-references) for each topic; several subsections are single short paragraphs or bullets only.

There are no explicit cross-reference placeholders (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Governance]') linking this general requirements section to the detailed Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, and Metrics and Targets sections.
IFRS pillars (Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics and Targets) are embedded as bullets under 'Connected information' rather than as explicit, consistently ordered subheadings.
wording_issues: The section hard-codes specific reporting period end date, years, jurisdictions, and currency, which conflicts with the style rule to avoid embedding fixed dates, years, currencies, and geographic footprints in reusable template text.
Some terms and acronyms (e.g., NGFS v4, NACE, EPC, LTV, CDP) are used without definition, contrary to the requirement to define key terms before first use.

Risk descriptions use narrative phrasing (e.g., 'could damage brand and trigger client attrition') without explicitly linking to financial statement areas or using the cause → mechanism → potential financial effect pathway language.

The section purpose (basis of preparation and 'how to read this report') is only partially addressed; there is limited explanation of reporting boundary, alignment with financial statements, or treatment of estimates and judgements.

Forward-looking or scenario-related content (e.g., 'Resilience assessments are performed under orderly and disorderly transition scenarios') is stated factually but could more clearly use cautious modality ('are intended to be performed', 'are expected to be performed') if there is any judgement or estimation involved.

The section does not explicitly distinguish between current-period facts, estimates, and forward-looking intentions; for example, scenario analysis and resilience assessments are described without clarifying whether they are current-period activities or ongoing practices.
table_figure_issues: No tables or figures are used, which is acceptable in principle, but the section could benefit from a compact table summarizing general requirement topics and cross-references, as suggested by the style guide.
Because there are no tables or figures, there are no captions or numbering; this is not a violation but does not leverage the recommended visual anchors for scanability.
required_fixes: Introduce a short opening paragraph that clearly states the basis of preparation and purpose of the section (e.g., that it explains how sustainability-related financial disclosures are prepared, scoped, and connected to the financial statements).

Convert headings to a numbered hierarchy consistent with the overall report structure (e.g., '1. General requirements', '1.1 Basis of preparation', '1.2 Reporting period and comparatives', '1.3 Fair presentation and material information', '1.4 Connected information', etc.).
Add one-sentence purpose statements at the start of each subsection to explain what is being disclosed and how users should interpret it.

Reframe narrative sentences to use standards-oriented disclosure verbs (e.g., 'We prepare these disclosures for the reporting period ending …', 'We disclose comparative information for …', 'We identify the following climate-related risks as material to our prospects').

Add lead-in sentences before bullet lists that clarify whether the bullets are examples, a subset, or a complete list of items (e.g., 'The climate risk register currently identifies the following material climate-related risks that could reasonably be expected to affect our prospects:').

Clarify and define acronyms and technical terms at first use (e.g., NGFS scenarios, NACE sector classification, EPC energy performance certificates, LTV loan-to-value, CDP disclosure) or add a cross-reference to a definitions/abbreviations section.

Avoid hard-coding specific dates, years, currencies, and jurisdiction lists in template-style narrative; where such specifics are necessary for this report, frame them as report-specific parameters and ensure they are not embedded in reusable boilerplate text.

Expand the 'Basis of preparation' and related subsections to describe alignment with the financial reporting boundary, treatment of estimates and judgements, and how sustainability-related information is connected to the primary financial statements, using cross-reference placeholders where detailed information is provided elsewhere.

Under 'Connected information', restructure content so that Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, and Metrics and Targets are either separate numbered subsections or clearly cross-referenced to their dedicated sections, rather than only appearing as bullets.

Where scenario analysis and resilience assessments are described, clarify whether they relate to the current reporting period and, if they involve estimates or forward-looking assumptions, use cautious modality and briefly note that they are subject to methodological uncertainty.

Add at least one brief closing sentence for the section (or major subsections) that provides connectivity to other parts of the report set (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Governance] for further detail on board oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities.').
style_judge.summary: The section is broadly aligned with a formal, neutral, IFRS-style disclosure voice and uses clear, concise sentences and appropriate bulleting. However, it does not fully follow the approved authoring style for a general requirements section. Key gaps include the absence of numbered headings and explicit purpose statements, limited explanation of basis of preparation and connectivity to financial statements, lack of cross-reference placeholders, and use of hard-coded dates, years, currency, and jurisdictions that conflict with the reusable-template guidance. Acronyms and technical terms are not defined at first use, and the IFRS pillars are not structured as explicit subsections. With these structural and wording adjustments, the section could be brought into full compliance with the style guide.
